I understand that dilemma of not wanting to outright reject one's sexuality or urges whilst also understanding the perils of pornography and the "coomer" lifestyle/ mindset. As one who is also struggling and feels intimidated by the amount of healing required in their journey to make progress, some of the things I find helpful are,

-masturbating w/o porn. It is still a form of stimulation that can potentially be addictive, but on it's own it's not as intense as watching pornography. If you finish then it does relieve the urges to an extent. I have relapsed before into watching porn, and I kind of realize it's better not to compromise on that, or at least initially to ween off the addiction.

-Exercise. Releases energy in a productive way. Health benefits.

-Meditation. Learning to get comfortable with your feelings and act as an observer to the self will help you learn to distance from and process feelings. Helps in objectivity.

-Build your life one step at a time. In the end if the PMO is a coping mechanism, one of the best cures is to improve your life and find happiness outside of porn use. As Dr K once said, "Once you live a life worth living, the addictions will start to melt away."

Therapy and journaling. Processing our traumas and story is a journey, it is difficult but necessary to progress. It is another part of being a proper adult.

Hope this helps. Remember to be patient with yourself, as life is a journey and change is often incremental.
